description:
**File**: `src/services/memory_manager_actor.cr:396-422`

**Severity**: P2 (architecture violation per architecture.md §1)

`clear_system_caches` enumerates every cache in the system by name:
- `VugAdapter.clear_cache`
- `Fetcher::DnsCache.clear_expired`
- `Fetcher::CrestHttpClient.clear_rate_limiters`
- `Fetcher::URLValidator.clear_validated`
- `Fetcher::CircuitBreaker::Registry.store.clear_expired`
- `ColorExtractor.sweep_cache`
- `QuickHeadlines::StringIntern.clear`
- `FaviconActor.instance.close_pooled_clients`
- `FaviconCache.clear`

This is the opposite of "replaceable modules" (`planning/architecture.md`
§1). Every time someone adds a new cache, they must update this
method. The Hash `@cleanup_handlers` already exists for exactly this
purpose but is not used here.

**Fix sketch**:
1. Move each cleanup call into a `register_cleanup_handler` cast
   from the subsystem itself (e.g., `StringIntern.register_cleanup`)
2. `clear_system_caches` becomes `run_registered_handlers(level)`
3. Subsystems own their cleanup; the actor only orchestrates

This is the plugin-architecture pattern explicitly called out in
`planning/architecture.md`.

Found during code review 2026-06-18, see
`planning/code-review-2026-06-18.md` §3.2.
title: MemoryManagerActor.clear_system_caches knows every cache (leaky abstraction)
